claims: "Pinch" originated from Middle English (pinchen) and Anglo-French (pinchier).
The earliest known use of the verb "pinch" is from around 1230.
In horticulture, pinching means removing buds/shoots to encourage growth.
A four-finger pinch is a quarter teaspoon.
"Pinching pennies" refers to extreme saving or being in a tight financial situation.
In slang, "pinch" means to be arrested.
A "pinch harmonic" is a guitar technique creating a high-pitched squeal.
"Edelrid Pinch" is a type of belay device in climbing.
Pinching causes pain because it compresses skin, nerves, and blood vessels together, triggering pain receptors (nociceptors) in the skin.
Pinching is sometimes used in medical contexts to test for dehydration (skin resiliency).
Pinching is used to measure body fat using skinfold calipers.
Two-finger pinch or finger and thumb pinch is the standard grip.
Four-finger pinch is used for measurements.
A pinch bar is used for heavy objects.
